sources.kmd: bc250-win a3435bc2 (train/b29), the b29 train driver 0.7.216.28. The release default of the automatic clock ceiling is 2000 MHz (owner decision 2026-10-10, fix/dpm-default-2000 9e313fe9 merged into the train): BC250_DPM_DEFAULT_MAX_MHZ is 2000u, the installer table writes DpmMaxMHz 2000 and moves a stored 1500 to it, the start clock stays 1000 MHz, the idle point stays 500 MHz and the hard ceiling, the thermal rules and the voltage band are unchanged. Two kernel wagons ride this train. The VRAM capacity report: the private caps blob of KMTQAITYPE_UMDRIVERPRIVATE carried the local and CPU-visible VRAM totals of the machine the contract capture was taken on, which is 8 GiB whatever the board reserves, and VramPatchCaps now writes the application segment's own Length into both words, from the same WddmMemoryLayout calculation that QUERYSEGMENT4 publishes, with the POST framebuffer, the reserved tail and the page-table storage excluded and zero in both words where the layout or the aperture admission is unavailable. The caps query reads start-latched geometry and touches no register. The board memory service: on a positively identified BC-250 the driver reads the board's memory reservation and, for an administrator at PASSIVE_LEVEL on a started and awake adapter, changes it between 8192 and 12288 MiB through the RUN_BOARD_MEMORY escape, command 32, operation ABI 2. Both HAL forms are checked at device start and again before a change, exactly one must pass, and a failed check leaves writes unavailable. The original 28-byte block is saved under Control\\amdgpu-wddm-board-memory with a protected DACL before the first write, the transaction invalidates the signature first and commits it last, a failure rolls back inside its own bound, and a pending record at a later start refuses every further change. Every other board answers that the control is not supported and performs no CMOS access. A platform-wide push lock serializes detection, persistence, write and teardown across adapter instances, and stop waits for the operation. No hardware acceptance is claimed: every gate of this wagon is a host gate on a machine without a board. Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.26: bc250-win 2fa44ac3 (train/b28), the b28 train driver 0.7.216.27, escape ABI 0x000700D8 (unchanged since 0.7.216.1). Two kernel wagons ride this train. BD-114, the private submit watchdog: the driver's own 500 ms budget for one graphics submission becomes SubmitWatchdogMs, whose default is TdrDelay plus 2000 ms (12000 ms with this release's TdrDelay of 10 s), clamped to five minutes and never shorter than TdrDelay itself, re-armed when the work makes progress, with the deadline at the head of the ring and measured times in the timeout line; an empty-ring recovery may name the completed fence as aborted only where the per-node completion and publication state is authoritative, and recovery admission waits up to 500 ms for an active submitter to leave with no spin lock held. On the lab, 2026-10-10, the dense model that bugchecked the shipped 500 ms build twice that morning ran to a complete result on these sources (gemma-4-12b-it-qat-q4_0, -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128 -r 3: 207.38 t/s prompt, 32.94 t/s generation, no timeout, no refusal, no recovery, no bugcheck). Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.25: bc250-win 349f1236 (train/b27), the b27 train driver 0.7.216.26, escape ABI 0x000700D8 (unchanged since 0.7.216.1). Three kernel changes ride this train. The fan load feed-forward (rule 10 of docs/design/fan.md): the governor hands the fan step a load feed beside the Tctl reading (GPU busy share weighted by each DPM tick's length, the governor's GFX clock level and the SMU socket power), a step is heavy at 850 permille busy above 1000 MHz, at 85 W, or at a 3 C rise over a 3 s window, 2 s of heavy time engages 100 % duty, the boost holds 30 s after the load and then waits for the curve itself to ask for less, and it never lowers a duty. FanLoadBoost 0 switches the rule off for the start, which the escape reports as BOOST_OFF; the record grows six flags and the fan log line says which signal called the load heavy. Audit finding F3: the CPU boost probe runs its whole bound and keeps the highest core clock it observed under load, instead of stopping at the first reply in band, because the firmware's core-frequency reply is the clock of the moment and promises no ceiling. Audit finding K1: the runtime DriverVersion write in the adapter's software key stays a closed deviation, the setting is absent after an install, no install of the package may name it (the inf-gates gate), and only the control application turns it on. sources.mft_h264: bc250-win 349f1236 (train/b27), the H.264 encoder MFT. Two changes against tester.24. Audit finding A5/UMD-2: DeviceLease::Take returns an HRESULT and the transform runs nothing without the lease. It passed nullptr for the device output of IMFDXGIDeviceManager::LockDevice and dropped the status of both OpenDeviceHandle and LockDevice, so a client that reset its device manager let our dispatches and the client's own work reach one device context at once while the transform reported success. S_OK now means the lease is held, or that there is no manager at all and the transform owns its device; a lock that writes no device is E_UNEXPECTED, and the device the manager hands back is kept for the life of the lease and released before the unlock. Audit finding A11/UMD-3: the dependency-safe Waves deblock schedule is the default again. The Rows schedule is one dispatch whose forward progress rests on all macroblock-row groups being resident at once, which Direct3D does not promise; when its spin budget ran out a group filtered anyway and published the same count an ordered row publishes, so the reconstruction drifted with no failure word anywhere. Waves synchronises at the dispatch boundary and assumes no residency, its order is arithmetic a test can read (DeblockWaveRows/DeblockWaveCount), and BC250_MFT_DEBLOCK=rows selects the single dispatch explicitly Carried from 0.7.216.100-tester.24: bc250-win 689852a8 (train/b20-setup), which carries e52/encoder-perf e4d1f630, the H.264 encoder transform; the respin does not rebuild it
sources.control_app: bc250-win a3435bc2 (train/b29), the control application with the board memory card. The release default of the automatic clock ceiling is 2000 MHz (owner decision 2026-10-10, fix/dpm-default-2000 9e313fe9 merged into the train): BC250_DPM_DEFAULT_MAX_MHZ is 2000u, the installer table writes DpmMaxMHz 2000 and moves a stored 1500 to it, the start clock stays 1000 MHz, the idle point stays 500 MHz and the hard ceiling, the thermal rules and the voltage band are unchanged. The card reads the active size and the next-start size apart, offers 8192 and 12288 MiB on a BC-250 only, explains the RAM trade-off, asks for an elevated confirmation that is bound to the block and the capabilities it was shown, offers a restart afterwards and never restarts Windows itself. An unknown next-start value is not drawn as zero and not as a pending change. Restore puts the saved original block back, not a value the client chose. On another adapter the card shows the memory size from the Windows segment statistics and says that the control is not supported. The board memory service: RUN_BOARD_MEMORY, command 32, operation ABI 2, with READ under NoAdapterSynchronization from a cached snapshot and SET or RESTORE behind the write capability, an administrator, HardwareAccess, PASSIVE_LEVEL and a started, awake adapter; both HAL forms are proved at start and again before a change, exactly one must pass, the RTC control never reads register C, the requested delay is at most three seconds, and a failed check leaves writes unavailable.
